issue.title: sase-listen: articles with H3-only sections render a single verbatim chapter (and the writer outline says none)

task_type_fields.impact:
Verbatim (`-e verbatim`) editions of H3-sectioned articles publish to AntennaPod as one
long chapter with no chapter skipping. This is common on openai.com index pages. Brief
and full editions are unaffected because the writer authors its own `##` chapters. The
writer's outline hint is empty for these pages, so it relies on the inline `###`
headings alone.
task_type_fields.repro:
Reproduce in a scratch XDG tree (no API calls, nothing published):

```bash
T=$(mktemp -d); export XDG_DATA_HOME=$T/data XDG_STATE_HOME=$T/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=$T/cache
URL=https://openai.com/index/open-source-codex-orchestration-symphony/
sase-listen script "$URL" -e verbatim --json   # "chapters": 1 chapter, 2361 words
sase-listen render "$URL" -e verbatim --dry-run # Chapters: 1 (16.0 min); W008 Chapter has 2361 words (> 900)
```

Observed on athena 2026-10-05 (sase-listen 0.1.0 with sase-1g7). The page's eight
section headings are `<h3>` (there is no `<h2>`). Trafilatura keeps them as `###`, so
`source.json` shows `outline: {found: 8, restored: [], missing: []}`.

Root cause, in two parts:

1. `normalize/normalizer.py` (the sase-1e3.3 script contract) turns only `##` headings
   into chapters. H3–H6 become a spoken sentence, so an article whose top section level
   is H3 collapses into a single chapter.
2. `web/store.py::_source_markdown` prepends `# {metadata title}` ("…Symphony." with a
   trailing period) ahead of Trafilatura's own page H1 ("…Symphony"). The normalizer
   consumes the first H1 as the title and opens the single chapter on the second,
   non-identical H1.

A related smaller issue: `writer/prompt.py::user_prompt` lists only `outline.restored`
headings. When the extractor already kept the headings (restored is empty), the
writer's outline says "(none)". The headings are still in the source text.

Suggested fix: for article sources, promote the shallowest section heading level to
`##` when the extracted Markdown has no `##` (in `_article_script`, or when building
`source.md`). Drop or merge a page H1 that only duplicates the metadata title. Pass
every found outline heading to the writer, not just the restored ones. Build synthetic
H3-only HTML for the tests; do not commit third-party article text as a fixture.

issue.creation_reason: Found while writing a sase-listen article-to-AntennaPod report: the Symphony article probe produced one 16-minute verbatim chapter instead of eight. Root cause is pinned to the H2-only chapter rule and the duplicated H1 in source.md.
